inlines.v: ANTANAGO'GE, noun antanago'gy. [Gr. against, and a taking up.] In rhetoric, a figure which consists in replying to an adversary, by way of recrimination; as, when the accusation of one party is unanswerable, the accused person charges him with the same or other crime.
